title: SWAG posterior subspace with stochastic Mirror coordinates

random_selection.pool_rule: latest baseline rows priority=P0 AND status=UNTESTED; exclude IDs with any live remote research/ma-* branch and any MA experiment directory in the baseline tree; preserve registry order

selected_row.proposal: SWAG covariance subspace -> Mirror posterior coordinates
selected_row.shared_object: shared mean model and low-rank covariance basis
selected_row.mirror_coordinate: stochastic Mirror coordinate in SWAG subspace
selected_row.mirror_delta: Represent posterior samples by structured low-dimensional View coordinates over one physical mean model.
selected_row.worker_note: Compare SWAG with the same covariance rank.

hypothesis: For an SGD-derived rank-r posterior subspace over a shared MLP mean, Rademacher Mirror coordinates over the same covariance basis can improve corruption-shift predictive NLL or calibration over native Gaussian SWAG coordinates without reducing clean quality or increasing actual payload bytes or K-member inference compute.
physical_object: One shared mean MLP plus SWAG low-rank covariance basis and diagonal scale.
mirror_coordinate: Per-member Rademacher vector m in {-1,+1}^r over the top-r SWAG covariance eigen-directions; independent diagonal Gaussian perturbation is shared between the Mirror and Gaussian SWAG parameterizations.
logical_multiplicity: K=8 sampled posterior-predictive classifiers generated from one shared mean and covariance state. Do not describe 2^r code combinations as independent capacity.
prior_art_delta: SWAG already samples a low-rank plus diagonal Gaussian posterior around one mean. Test only the extra value of a structured discrete Mirror coordinate over the same covariance rank. Rank-1 Bayesian factor perturbation and independent checkpoints are controls.
controls: Gaussian low-rank SWAG posterior with matching rank and diagonal variance
post-hoc rank-1 multiplicative factor posterior with dev-selected global scale

development.dataset: sklearn load_digits; fixed stratified train/dev split from source/dataset_manifest.json
conditions: Gaussian pixel corruption sigma=0.25, clamped to [0,1]
development.selection_metric: corruption-shift NLL with clean NLL/ECE guardrails; actual serialized bytes and K=8 wall time

training_protocol.optimizer_updates_per_fit: 80 epochs over the fixed training split; actual batch count recorded
training_protocol.snapshots: final 20 epoch states for SWAG mean/covariance
training_protocol.randomness: all train/sample seeds frozen; posterior sample count K=8

paid_objects: full diagonal standard deviations for SWAG and Mirror

gates.development_pass: For at least one rank and both development training seeds: Mirror clean NLL no more than +0.02 over matched Gaussian SWAG; shifted NLL at least 0.02 lower OR shifted ECE at least 0.01 lower; clean ECE no more than +0.01; whole serialized payload <= matched SWAG; K=8 predictive wall time <=1.05x SWAG; and improvement repeats on both seeds.
gates.mirror_specific: The same rank-matched Gaussian SWAG is the decisive control. A Rademacher coordinate change must meet the shifted improvement clause; matching outputs/metrics does not count as Mirror-specific.
gates.fresh_opening: Open the locked fresh split only if one rank passes all development clauses on both seeds. Otherwise FAIL and do not inspect audit labels/metrics.

boundaries: No capacity claim; fixed K=8 posterior predictive screen
Rank-1 factor control is post-hoc global-scale calibration, not a full reproduction of the Rank-1 BNN paper
No claim that logical code count equals independent model capacity
Audit/fresh split remains locked unless the frozen gate passes
